score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by explicit commercial demand: North Carolina Board of Cosmetic Art Examiners and South Carolina Board of Cosmetology both list 'Mailing List Requests' and 'Licensee List Request' as official services, proving that B2B buyers routinely purchase these lists for marketing purposes. Four high-value buyer segments: (1) beauty and wellness product vendors (professional hair color brands like Redken, Wella, Schwarzkopf; skin care lines like Dermalogica, SkinCeuticals; massage equipment suppliers) selling B2B to licensed professionals with $500-$5,000/year spend per professional, (2) continuing education providers (state-required CE for license renewal in 40+ states, ranging from 6-16 hours every 1-2 years at $50-$300 per course), (3) professional liability insurance carriers (salon/spa E&O policies, massage therapist malpractice insurance at $200-$800/year per policy), and (4) staffing and recruiting agencies placing estheticians, massage therapists, and cosmetologists in spas, salons, medical spas, hotels, and cruise lines. All 50 states plus DC maintain public license registries via State Boards of Cosmetology, Massage Therapy Boards, or Departments of Licensing with downloadable or scrapable data including licensee name, license number, status, expiration date, and city/state. Zero PII — all professional credential data. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 51 state boards across 3 license types (cosmetology, esthetics, massage therapy), deduplicate dual-licensed professionals, and normalize specialty flags (nail tech, barber, medical esthetician, etc.). No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad. Audience size is massive: approximately 1.2 million cosmetologists, 100,000+ estheticians, and 400,000+ massage therapists nationwide (per BLS 2026 data), creating a TAM of 10,000+ B2B buyers (product vendors, CE providers, insurers, recruiters). Score is 7 due to explicit state board confirmation of commercial mailing list demand, validated willingness-to-pay across four distinct buyer segments, confirmed public data availability, and absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives.

data_wanted: All 50 states plus DC maintain public license registries for cosmetology, esthetics, and massage therapy via State Boards of Cosmetology, State Boards of Massage Therapy, Departments of Licensing, or combined professional licensing boards. Some states (North Carolina and South Carolina confirmed) explicitly provide 'Mailing List Requests' or 'Licensee List Request' services. Others offer online lookup portals requiring scraping. No authentication required. Key fields per license: professional full name (first, middle initial, last), license type (cosmetologist, esthetician, nail technician, barber, massage therapist, instructor, etc.), license number (format varies by state, typically 4-8 digits or alphanumeric), license status (active, inactive, lapsed, expired, suspended, revoked), original issue date, current expiration or renewal date, practice city and state (some states list full address, others only city/state or county), and specialty or advanced certifications where publicly listed (medical esthetician, oncology massage, advanced nail tech, etc.). Target all active licenses only (exclude inactive, expired, or revoked unless buyer explicitly needs re-licensing outreach). Scope to individual practitioners — exclude salon/spa business licenses (which are separate entity registrations). Approximate counts per license type: 1.2 million cosmetologists (hair stylists, colorists, salon owners), 100,000-150,000 estheticians (skin care specialists, medical estheticians, waxing specialists), 400,000-500,000 massage therapists (LMT, CMT depending on state), 200,000+ nail technicians, 100,000+ barbers. Total target output: 1.7-2.0 million rows across all three license types. Data is 100% public per state professional licensing statutes (licensing records are public information under state sunshine laws and Freedom of Information Acts).
